commits.subject: Report active client process exit failures (#5194)
commits.body:
## Summary

- classify generic client-worker exit code `1` as
`ProcessExitCode.EXCEPTION` only when the worker previously checked in
as `STARTED` and no parent-side abort was requested
- preserve the existing `STARTING + 1` infrastructure-failure
classification
- leave post-`STOPPED` teardown errors, launcher `UNKNOWN`, and explicit
abort paths unchanged

## Why

An in-process Client API trainer runs inside the client job worker. If
it terminates the process unexpectedly with exit code `1`, the client
parent observes a generic `JobReturnCode.EXECUTION_ERROR` while the
worker is still recorded as `STARTED`.

Since #4595, that generic code is not an authoritative server-side
failure. Both affected clients can disappear without failing the server
job, leaving it `RUNNING` until an external timeout or dead-client
fallback intervenes.

This patch restores bounded failure only at the active-worker boundary.
It does not make all generic launcher errors reportable:

| Parent observation | Effective outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `STARTING + EXECUTION_ERROR`, no abort | `INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR`
(existing behavior) |
| `STARTED + EXECUTION_ERROR`, no abort | `EXCEPTION` |
| `STOPPED + EXECUTION_ERROR` | unchanged, non-reportable teardown
result |
| explicit parent abort + `EXECUTION_ERROR` | unchanged, not promoted to
an application exception |
| launcher `UNKNOWN` | unchanged |
| canonical process failure or `ABORTED` | unchanged |

## Scope

The change is intentionally parent-side and limited to the reported
regression. It does not change `ClientRunner`, worker shutdown,
process-RC markers, workspace publication or extraction, Client API
backends, job launchers, or server failure mapping.

Client status notifications remain best effort. If a completed worker
loses its `STOPPED` notification and later exits with code `1`, the
parent can still observe stale `STARTED` state. A reliable completion
handshake is a separate lifecycle problem; this patch chooses bounded
failure for an apparently active worker rather than broadening the 2.9
fix into a new completion protocol.

## Testing

- exact two-client in-process reproduction: job reached
`FINISHED:EXECUTION_EXCEPTION` in 11.9 seconds instead of timing out
- focused client/server regression suite: `146 passed`
- full style check: `./runtest.sh -s --skip-install`
- `git diff --check`

Co-authored-by: Chester Chen <512707+chesterxgchen@users.noreply.github.com>
commits.root_cause: Active STARTED worker RC1 was not authoritative; promote to EXCEPTION unless parent abort. STOPPED notification loss remains explicitly best effort.

commits.subject: Finalize failed jobs with missing client outcomes (#5221)
commits.body:
## Summary

- release pending client outcomes when a stopped server job already has
an authoritative non-`ABORTED` failure
- preserve the existing outcome barrier for normal completion and
launcher `ABORTED` precedence
- add focused regression coverage for a server execution failure with a
pending client outcome

## Root cause

The completion loop checked the pending-client outcome barrier before
evaluating an already-recorded server-process failure. A client that
became unreachable could therefore keep a known failed job in `RUNNING`
until the normal outcome or heartbeat timeout expired.

## Validation

- `176 passed` across focused server/client lifecycle tests
- `./runtest.sh -s`
- `git diff --check`

Fixes #5220.

---------

Signed-off-by: Peter Cnudde <pcnudde@nvidia.com>

commits.subject: Fix concurrent job lifecycle accounting (#5216)
commits.body:
## Summary

- publish the originating job ID as non-sticky data on server job
lifecycle events
- make `DefaultJobScheduler` prefer the explicit event job ID while
preserving the existing sticky-ID fallback
- add regression coverage for sticky context changes and
start/completion/abort publication

## Problem

Concurrent job launch and completion processing can replace the sticky
`CURRENT_JOB_ID` before a lifecycle event handler reads it. The
scheduler can then account a start, completion, or abort against the
wrong job, leaving stale entries in `scheduled_jobs`. Once those entries
reach `max_jobs`, valid admissions can be blocked even though execution
capacity is available.

## Validation

- `72 passed` in the focused scheduler and JobRunner unit-test suites
- Black, isort, and Flake8 passed for all four changed files
- `git diff --check` passed
- a 100-job, one-server/two-client validation with `max_jobs=20`
completed all jobs successfully, with each job scheduled exactly once
and no stale-accounting serial tail

Fixes #5215
commits.root_cause: Sticky CURRENT_JOB_ID could switch under concurrent scheduling/completion; publish explicit non-sticky event job ID and prefer it in scheduler.

commits.subject: Treat duplicate mandatory clients as one required site (#5161)
commits.body:
## Summary

- deduplicate mandatory clients before scheduler admission while
preserving their first-seen order
- allow harmless duplicate entries to schedule when the required site is
connected and has sufficient resources
- block non-string mandatory-client entries before study-enrollment
membership checks
- add regression coverage for duplicate and malformed mandatory-client
entries

## Root cause

`DefaultJobScheduler._try_job()` copied `job.required_sites` into a list
of sites still needing resources. A successful resource check removed
only one matching entry, so a duplicate remained and incorrectly
triggered the required-site no-resource path.

Malformed non-string entries also exposed hash-based failure paths
during deduplication and study-enrollment lookup, which could interrupt
a scheduling pass before later valid candidates were considered.

## Impact

Mandatory-client membership now has set semantics during scheduling.
Invalid entries are blocked as job-definition errors without starving
later candidates. Existing required-site diagnostics retain list
formatting and deterministic order, and the resource cancellation and
retry paths are unchanged.

This is pre-existing behavior discovered while reviewing #5149; that PR
did not introduce the bug.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest
tests/unit_test/app_common/job_schedulers/job_scheduler_test.py -v` — 23
passed
- scoped `black --check`, `isort --check`, and `flake8` for both changed
files
- `git diff --check`
commits.root_cause: Duplicate mandatory client names falsely remained unsatisfied; deduplicate and reject non-string entries before membership checks.

commits.subject: Harden Client API and Swarm abort cleanup (#5097)
commits.body:
## Summary

Fix #5099.

- Bound live accepted-result cleanup to the END_RUN acknowledgement
interval instead of the longer streaming timeout.
- Force-stop every still-owned trainer process group after that bound
without adding a second termination grace.
- Pass the owning Client Job PID to launched trainers and monitor it so
abrupt CJ exit cannot orphan the trainer process group.
- Propagate graceful job abort to an external backend even after
`execute()` returned an accepted lazy result, so aborted teardown does
not preserve a live result source.
- Fail a job promptly when an owned external trainer dies after its lazy
result was accepted, interrupting the exact receiver download instead of
entering the 600-second retry path.
- Preserve user-abort precedence so late process exits cannot reclassify
`FINISHED:ABORTED` as an execution failure.
- Order result archival, terminal failure reporting, F3 shutdown, and
process cleanup so terminal state is authenticated and authoritative.
- Make active CCWF work abort at `ABOUT_TO_END_RUN`, including work not
represented in `ClientRunner.running_tasks`.
- Carry the run abort signal into Swarm's explicit lazy-reference
decode, cancel active disk tensor consumers under the job-scoped root,
serialize cleanup with chunk writes, and reject writes after cleanup.
- Add a capability-negotiated receiver cancellation handshake so an
abandoned download settles the producer's accepted result transaction
promptly, including all sibling refs for that receiver.
- Keep Attach mode exempt from owned-process monitoring because its
trainer process is externally owned.

## Change structure and scope

The accepted-result-source contract is Client API-specific, while part
of the implementation hardens shared job-process lifecycle
infrastructure that is used by every CJ and SJ:

1. **Client API-specific source lifecycle.** The Client API protocol and
backends track an accepted lazy result source until receiver settlement,
detect owned trainer exit/disconnect, notify the exact DownloadService
receiver, interrupt the affected reference without entering
`DOWNLOAD_RETRY`, distinguish explicit run abort from source failure,
and clean active and retired `launch_once=false` trainer groups. Attach
sessions close without killing their externally owned trainer.
2. **Shared CJ/SJ lifecycle prerequisites.** Generic command-callback
admission and the job-process teardown pipeline reject new callbacks,
archive while F3 is still available, stop F3/Cell, drain admitted
callbacks, and close audit/security state in that order. Generic
child-outcome delivery reports an authoritative process result before
logout, and a logically `STOPPED` but still-live child remains
reclaimable. These races predate Client API, but the accepted-source
fatal path exercises them deterministically; removing this cluster
breaks the failure contract above.
3. **Generic server completion hardening.** Workflow submission
admission is serialized with server-runner completion so late
task/result callbacks cannot enter already-finalized state.

The deliberate behavior change is that loss of an already accepted lazy
source is run-fatal: it reaches `FINISHED:EXECUTION_EXCEPTION` even when
controller response thresholds might otherwise tolerate a missing
client. A user-requested abort remains authoritative and reaches
`FINISHED:ABORTED`.

Crash-safe tensor scratch reclamation after abrupt SJ/CJ death is not
implemented here. This PR guarantees owned trainer-process-group cleanup
after abrupt CJ death, but not reclamation of a tensor offload directory
owned only by a killed job process. The removed parent-tempdir discovery
approach was local-launcher-only, could not cross Docker/Kubernetes
mount namespaces, and tied reclamation to one parent PID. The P0
follow-up will use launcher-provisioned, parent-owned job scratch whose
cleanup capability survives process/container boundaries and parent
restart.

## Problems

### Late accepted Client API results

For `launch_once=false`, a trainer that publishes a late result can
outlive its owning Client Job process when the server has already
accepted enough responses. The result-source reaper could wait longer
than the outer CJ teardown budget, allowing the CJ to exit first and
leave the trainer process group orphaned.

If an owned trainer crashes or is OOM-killed after `RESULT_READY` is
accepted, its lazy source can disappear while FedAvg or Swarm is still
downloading tensors. Previously the receiver kept retrying the
permanently unavailable source for the normal streaming timeout, leaving
the workflow RUNNING. This PR propagates the exact accepted-source loss
through DownloadService and the workflow's existing error path,
producing a bounded `FINISHED:EXECUTION_EXCEPTION` result.

### Graceful Swarm abort during tensor offload

A graceful abort can arrive while a remote multi-GB contribution is
being materialized under the aggregation client's tensor disk-offload
root. Swarm performs that terminal materialization through an explicit
FOBS round trip outside `Cell.decode_payload()`; its fresh decode
context did not carry the run abort signal. Cleanup waited only for
controller-owned learning/aggregation threads, while the active download
could be writing from an AUX/streaming handler thread.

An external trainer whose lazy result had already been accepted can also
outlive the nested workflow task that originally launched it. In that
state `ABORT_TASK` may no longer reach the backend, and stopping only
the receiver leaves the producer waiting for its ordinary
accepted-source drain. The receiver therefore needs a transaction-level
way to report that it abandoned an acquired download.

## Lifecycle contract

Normal END_RUN gives an accepted live result source one short
acknowledged SHUTDOWN interval so truthful publication can settle, then
force-cleans every still-owned process group.

Graceful abort propagates to the active workflow, lazy tensor download,
disk consumer, and external trainer. Once a receiver has learned that
its producer supports cancellation, abandoning the download sends
terminal receiver failure back to the producer. The producer applies
that failure to every ref for the same receiver in the transaction,
allowing the accepted source to settle without the normal drain timeout.
Cancellation is identity- and acquisition-checked; mixed-version peers
retain the existing bounded timeout fallback.

An accepted-source loss is run-fatal: it interrupts the matching
download and uses the controller's failure path even when a controller
could otherwise tolerate fewer responses. A user-requested run abort
remains authoritative over a racing process failure.

Root deletion occurs only after active consumers are cancelled and
in-flight chunk writes leave their serialized critical section.
Source-loss panic follows normal workflow teardown, so live
server/client job processes remove their own roots before exit.

## Validation

- Current PR head: signed `36e5ff529283d0c3c827c010f443256e8cf4132b`
(tree `a1d21aa33abf339c1d3114b39381d63af3bf984e`).
- GitHub CI is green on the current head, including Linux unit matrices
for Python 3.10 through 3.14 on Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04, coverage, style,
CodeQL, wheel build, documentation links, skill validation, and
maintained Hugging Face compatibility checks.
- Current split: 46 focused lifecycle/offload regressions passed.
- Current affected-area suite on the merged head: 1,140 passed, 1
skipped.
- Full repository Black, isort, flake8, and agent-skill checks passed.
- Unit coverage includes duplicate/idempotent cancellation,
multi-receiver and sibling-ref accounting, cancellation racing an
in-flight serve, first-reply and pipelined aborts, source connection
loss, consumer I/O failure, failed cancel delivery, normal completion
without cancellation, SIGKILL of an accepted-result trainer,
authoritative RC-file preservation, bounded STOPPED-worker cleanup
grace, and source-loss panic reaching END_RUN/root removal.
- Current-head GPU system qualification is still in progress. The
unchanged maintained `client_api` manifest has one observed failure in
`lightning-scaffold-client-api`: both DDP rank-1 processes receive
`api=None` during `flare.init()`. The same failure reproduced on
predecessor PR head `5db3b3b2`; an unchanged comparison on merged-main
parent `be2c91b733440aeb0eebe3191b10932e2d18a3e9` is queued to classify
whether it is pre-existing or introduced by this PR. This item is not
claimed as passed.
- Exact signed predecessor-head lifecycle E2E: trainer SIGKILL after
accepted lazy result and active disk download reached
`FINISHED:EXECUTION_EXCEPTION` in 9.31 seconds, preserved/consumed
RC101, emitted the authenticated failure report, interrupted the exact
download without `DOWNLOAD_RETRY`, fired all END_RUN events, and removed
job processes and roots.
- Prior exact signed-head E2E: graceful active-transfer abort reached
`FINISHED:ABORTED` with all required END_RUN events and no process,
root, descriptor, socket, or GPU residue through delayed audits.
- Exact signed predecessor-head normal-control E2E: full six-round Swarm
completion and a separate subsequent canary both reached
`FINISHED:COMPLETED` and cleaned resources.
- Abrupt SJ/CJ scratch-directory reclamation and cross-launcher scratch
ownership are explicitly out of scope for this PR and must be qualified
in the launcher-owned scratch follow-up.

Fixes #5099.

commits.subject: Harden resource admission failure handling (#5149)
commits.body:
## Description

- tolerate resource managers returning no reservation token for a
required-site rejection
- keep the normal cancellation, scheduling-history, retry-backoff, and
maximum-attempt path intact
- remove the unused return code from the resource-check response body
- strengthen the existing required-site test so it cannot pass through
the scheduler's broad exception handler

## Root cause

The required-site error message concatenated the reservation token
without handling `None`. A resource manager returning `(False, None)`
raised `TypeError` before cancellation and scheduling bookkeeping could
run. Separately, the client set a return code inside the response
`Shareable`, but the server reads only the outer admin message return
code and the resource token.

## Impact

Required-site resource rejection now follows the intended no-resource
path even when no token is returned. Resource-manager exception details
remain site-local, and the cross-site diagnostic behavior introduced in
#5148 is unchanged.

## Validation

- `22 passed`: focused scheduler and client resource-check unit tests
- `./runtest.sh -s`
- `git diff --check`

commits.subject: Surface resource manager admission errors (#5143)
commits.body:
## Description

Resource-manager exceptions during job admission were converted into a
generic `not enough sites have enough resources` result. This made
incompatible or malformed resource requirements look like temporary
capacity shortages and left operators without the underlying
site-specific reason.

This change:

- securely records resource-manager exceptions in the client log and
resource-check response
- includes non-empty site-specific rejection reasons in job scheduling
history
- clarifies that `resource_spec["@default"]` applies to every targeted
client and the server, while named client or `server` blocks
shallow-override individual fields
- keeps resource normalization and admission behavior unchanged

Jobs that do not match their configured resource manager remain
rejected, but the responsible site and reason are now visible instead of
being silently reduced to a generic capacity message.

commits.subject: Preserve workspace sources during archival (#5111)
commits.body:
## Summary

- build multi-source workspace archives directly from their source files
instead of moving those files into a temporary directory
- include final archive publication in the storage error-handling
boundary so failed publishes clean up their temporary archive
- publish with `os.replace()`, matching NVFlare's atomic-replacement
pattern
- add regression coverage for archive layout, ZIP-write failure, retry
completeness, final-publication failure, source preservation, and
diagnostics

## Root cause

`FilesystemStorage._write_multi` moved workspace contents into a
`TemporaryDirectory` before creating the ZIP. If ZIP creation failed—for
example because the job store was full, read-only, or returned an I/O
error—the context manager deleted that temporary directory and therefore
deleted the only copies of the workspace artifacts.

The retry then saw the original source directories still present but
empty, created an empty ZIP, and could publish the job as completed with
no trained model.

This is a follow-up to #5091. That fix prevents a cleanup retry from
overwriting an archive after `save_workspace` returns, but cannot cover
a failure inside `save_workspace` before its success latch is set.

## Impact

Packaging now treats list-based workspace sources as read-only. A failed
ZIP write or failed final publication leaves the source artifacts intact
for a complete retry, while a successful save is still followed by the
existing explicit JobRunner cleanup. This avoids both data loss and the
disk/RAM duplication that copying all sources into another staging
directory would introduce.

The existing documented `mv_file=True` behavior for single string-path
inputs is intentionally unchanged and outside this PR's scope.

## Validation

Authoritative validation used a fresh isolated checkout of the exact
signed PR head:

- head `be96c4082633bbab2fa5f4d61b8d01e7bdaef5b4`
- tree `4aee7b1e0e3f65daefed2f553004e1e44d12a5c5`
- parent `c3008e2e12e2db89730f1d953ec65671872f07c7`
- base `de7177fc6b98b71c1fdf931facd0d836879be7af`
- base..HEAD binary diff SHA-256
`9fddffb4db890faf5b14eca112c69a1878add71fcbd7b4d8b0ba78a88285427f`
- review-only parent..HEAD diff SHA-256
`c423e01447503c4c261f05eb5e553eac48ed0a89450aa583223ece53692c638e`
- Good EDDSA signature, clean source and unchanged QA, exact runtime
imports

Checks:

- `storage_test.py`: 32 passed, RC 0
- repository-wide Black, isort, flake8, agent-skill lint, and `git diff
--check`: passed
- GitHub CI: all unit-test matrices, coverage, style, CodeQL, wheel
build, compatibility, link, license, and review checks passed
- unchanged DLQASH MR !199 primary: 1 passed, RC 0
- persistent and transient companion selectors: 2 passed, RC 0
- supplemental overwrite/same-device `os.replace` diagnostic: passed

Primary Colossus job `941cb3c6-c5c3-45ed-a17e-535af71725a1`:

- job store locked for 25 seconds; 17 packaging writes failed while the
sources remained intact
- repaired retry reached `FINISHED:COMPLETED` in 25.004361 seconds
- final downloads: metadata 895 bytes, job archive 20,024 bytes,
workspace archive 101,234 bytes
- extracted workspace: 19 files / 98,208 bytes
- original 164-byte trained model survived with SHA-256
`ecb50e4ceb5147bc97cb674067d6e23bce6d6533ef18d8f5a05d29b8b6f59a25`
- no temporary archives, job-store entries, processes, listeners, or
CLOSE-WAIT sockets remained

Controls:

- persistent job-store failure: 60 expected failures, exact 60-second
bounded-grace message, source residue preserved, then completed after
permissions were restored
- transient failure: recovered after 2 expected failures in 10.968770
seconds; `ARCHIVAL_ABANDONED=no`; complete archive downloaded
successfully
- temporary host configuration was restored byte-for-byte after testing

## Review disposition

The duplicate-member compatibility question is closed as benign. When
two source roots contain the same relative member name, the new archive
contains both physical members; Python ZIP name lookup and extraction
select the later member, preserving the previous implementation's
effective last-wins result, while directory-name collisions no longer
destroy either source. No dedup prepass is included in this focused
data-loss fix. A separate hardening change could emit only the last
member if duplicate-member warnings or archive-scanner compatibility
become a requirement.

Review feedback on atomic replacement and diagnostics is addressed in
`be96c408`:

- final publication uses `os.replace()`
- unsupported content errors list `bytes`, `str`, and `list`
- invalid list entries report the offending path
- regression tests cover all three behaviors

Two pre-existing storage atomicity defects remain intentionally outside
this focused PR:

- for string content with `mv_file=True`, the source has already moved
to `tmp_path` when final publication runs; on publication failure,
cleanup now removes that only copy instead of leaving a manually
salvageable UUID temporary file. A dedicated follow-up should restore
`tmp_path` to the original source path, or deliberately preserve it, and
cover both recovery and destination preservation with failure injection.
- metadata publication failure during `create_object(...,
overwrite_existing=True)` can remove data and invalidate the previous
object.

These should be handled independently with dedicated failure-injection
coverage.

commits.subject: Harden job-controlled Docker launcher options (#5108)
commits.body:
## What changed

- add an explicit allowlist for Docker options supplied through job
metadata
- require locally authorized BYOC for job-controlled `entrypoint`,
alongside `image` and `python_path`
- reject host namespaces, privileges, capabilities, devices, mounts,
networks, and security options from both `launcher_spec` and legacy
nested `resource_spec`
- enforce the same policy again in `DockerJobLauncher` before calling
`containers.run()`
- preserve site-owned Docker configuration through
`default_job_container_kwargs` and study `docker_kwargs`
- propagate the deploy-derived local BYOC decision to both client and
server launcher paths
- add a 2.9 migration note and update Docker launcher documentation and
regression coverage

## Why

A job could select `launcher_spec.<site|default>.docker.entrypoint`
while relying on a trusted site-configured study image. BYOC derivation
only considered `image` and `python_path`, and the launcher forwarded
other Docker SDK kwargs without an allowlist. This let a submitter
override the trusted image's startup contract without BYOC permission
and exposed isolation-sensitive Docker controls to job metadata.

## Impact

Sites retain control over privileged and isolation-changing container
options. Jobs can still request the allowlisted options `image`,
`python_path`, `entrypoint`, `num_of_gpus`, and `shm_size`; executable
selection requires BYOC authorization at each receiving site.

This deliberately breaks jobs that previously supplied arbitrary Docker
SDK kwargs. Site-owned settings such as `ipc_mode` and `device_requests`
must move to `default_job_container_kwargs` or study `docker_kwargs`.
Stored jobs are revalidated at launch and may require metadata migration
after upgrade.

## Validation

- server-path regression covers deploy-authorized default `entrypoint`,
fail-closed BYOC removal, and missing deployed metadata
- focused changed-path suite — 296 passed
- broader launcher/server/client authorization suites — 982 passed
- `./runtest.sh -s --skip-install` — black, isort, flake8, and
agent-skill lint passed
- `git diff --check` passed

commits.subject: Wait for client terminal outcomes before finalizing jobs (#5072)
commits.body:
## Summary

- have each client report its terminal child-process outcome, including
success, through the existing server topic
- wait for active client outcomes before publishing the server terminal
job status
- apply reported failures before releasing the reporting client from the
completion barrier
- bound that wait with a configurable grace, then warn about unresolved
clients and finalize from the server known outcome
- resolve missing client outcomes conservatively through existing
heartbeat and dead-client handling

## Root cause

Server-side process exit was treated as sufficient evidence that the
distributed job had completed. A client could detect result-publication
failure only afterward, when the server had already published and cached
`FINISHED:COMPLETED`. The existing fire-and-forget path reported only
selected failure exit codes and did not participate in terminal-status
ordering.

## Repair

This reuses the existing terminal-outcome message and adds one
pending-client set per job. Each client makes one acknowledged
terminal-outcome report. `JobRunner` defers finalization until the set
is empty, and the server applies failure or abort classification before
removing the reporting client. Admin abort bypasses the barrier, missing
or dead clients are resolved through existing reconciliation paths, and
authenticated late or duplicate reports receive an idempotent `OK`.

`JobRunner` starts an in-memory per-job deadline.
`client_outcome_wait_timeout` is configurable in the application
configuration and defaults to 900 seconds. On expiry, the server logs
the unresolved client names, releases the barrier, and runs the existing
server-side status calculation; expiry does not synthesize a failure.

The change adds no client retry policy, persisted deadline, or new
protocol abstraction.

commits.body:
## What changed

- Force `MainProcessMonitor` to terminate with the computed process
return code even when the RC file cannot be written.
- Preserve deliberate NVFlare child exit codes (`EXCEPTION`,
`UNSAFE_COMPONENT`, and `CONFIG_ERROR`) from the selected K8s job
container.

propagation.

## Why

In no-shared-PVC K8s jobs, result-publication failure can remove the run
directory before shutdown. The RC-file write then fails and previously
skipped the force-exit call; in a container, self-SIGKILL is also not a
reliable PID 1 shutdown mechanism. Once the pod did terminate, the K8s
launcher flattened every failed pod to `ABORTED`, discarding deliberate
child process codes and changing the terminal job classification
relative to subprocess and shared-workspace modes.

This change makes the child exit reliably and carries deliberate NVFlare
failure codes through the K8s job handle so the existing parent
lifecycle can classify them correctly.

FLARE-3094. It does not redesign the separate client-side timing issue
where result-publication failure can be reported after the server has
already finalized the job.

commits.subject: Preserve successful Slurm results during heartbeat cleanup (#5019)
commits.body:
## Summary

- distinguish heartbeat cleanup from user or administrator aborts along
the private client job path
- let the Slurm launcher cancel stale work without recording user-abort
intent
- preserve the existing termination behavior for all non-Slurm launchers
and keep public APIs unchanged

## Root cause

After a job completes, the server can stop tracking it before the Slurm
client parent observes the terminal accounting record. A heartbeat in
that window asks the client to clean up the apparently stale job. That
cleanup previously called the same Slurm `terminate()` path as a real
user abort, setting `user_abort=True`. When delayed accounting later
reported `COMPLETED` with exit code 0, the stored abort intent overrode
the successful result and the client reported the job as failed.

The cleanup origin is now carried through private client implementation
methods. Slurm handles that origin without setting user-abort intent,
while a real abort still maps a clean cooperative exit to `ABORTED`.

commits.subject: Preserve abort requests during client job launch (#4910)
commits.body:
## Summary

- register a pending job handle before invoking the client job launcher
- preserve early terminate requests and forward them after the real
handle is attached
- make pre-attach polling report the job as still running and protect
launch registration ownership

## Why

Client job launchers can block before returning a usable job handle.
Previously, the job was not added to `run_processes` until after
`launch_job()` returned, so an abort received during that window saw the
app as stopped and was discarded. The job could then finish launching
and continue despite the abort request.

The pending handle makes the launch visible as `STARTING`, remembers an
early terminate request, and forwards it as soon as the launcher returns
its real handle. It also removes its registration if launch fails
without disturbing another owner.

This preserves abort intent; it does not interrupt the launcher's
synchronous submission call, so cancellation remains bounded by launch
latency.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest
tests/unit_test/private/fed/client/client_executor_test.py -v` (25
passed)
- `./runtest.sh -s`

contract for aborted jobs.

packaging default result components, so direct Flare API callers receive

commits.subject: [2.8] Fix JobLogReceiver not registering in server-job subprocess (#4586)
commits.body:
## Summary

Restores live log streaming on the 2.8 branch. After #4558 the receiver
silently stops registering its `log_streaming:live_log` handler in
per-job server subprocesses, so every chunk from a client's
`JobLogStreamer` is rejected with:

```
ObjectStreamer - ERROR - [tx_id='…' channel='log_streaming' topic='live_log' seq=0] no stream processing info registered for log_streaming:live_log
_LogTailProducer - ERROR - error from target server: EXECUTION_EXCEPTION
```

The bootstrap-tolerant retry from #4558 hides the first 10 chunks and
then surfaces the ERROR, so it looks like a teardown race in short jobs;
on a longer job the first heartbeat (default `liveness_interval=10s`)
fires mid-run, well before any shutdown — which is what tipped this off.

## Root cause

`JobLogReceiver.__init__` registers `_register` on
`[SYSTEM_START, ABOUT_TO_START_RUN]`. Neither event fires in the
server-job subprocess spawned by `ServerProcessJobLauncher`:

- `SYSTEM_START` is only fired by `server_deployer.deploy()`, which the
  parent process runs. The subprocess enters through
  `nvflare/private/fed/app/server/runner_process.py:99`
  (`deployer.create_fl_server(...)`, **not** `deploy()`).
- `ABOUT_TO_START_RUN` is only fired in
  `nvflare/private/fed/client/client_runner.py:739` — client-side only.

The only server-job lifecycle event is `START_RUN`
(`nvflare/private/fed/server/server_runner.py:188`), which the receiver
no longer listens to. Result: the subprocess's `JobLogReceiver` instance
has `_registered=False` for the entire job and never calls
`engine.register_stream_processing`, leaving the run's
`ObjectStreamer.registry` empty for the live-log channel.

The `_registered` latch is also wrong for in-process deployments where
`engine.set_run_manager(...)` swaps in a new
`RunManager`/`ObjectStreamer`
per job: registering once against the parent's streamer would leave each
new job's registry empty even if the trigger events did fire.

## Fix

`nvflare/app_common/logging/job_log_receiver.py`:

1. Trigger `_register` on **`SYSTEM_START`, `ABOUT_TO_START_RUN`, and
   `START_RUN`** so the receiver wires up wherever it happens to live.
2. Drop the `_registered` early-return — `Registry.set` is idempotent
   for the same channel/topic, and re-registering after a run-manager
   swap is the desired behavior.

Docstring updated to describe the new placement-aware behavior.

## Why this shape

- **Restores the original (pre-#4558) server-subprocess behavior.** The
  bootstrap-tolerant `_LogTailProducer.process_replies` from #4558 is
  the actual fix for the client/server startup race; the
  `START_RUN` → `ABOUT_TO_START_RUN` event change was only listed as
  "defense in depth" and turns out to disable registration entirely in
  the subprocess. Reverting just the event list keeps the real fix
  intact.
- **Surgical.** Two-file change, no churn outside `JobLogReceiver`.
- **Forward-compatible.** Listing all three events also covers
  in-process deployments where the run manager is swapped per job.

## Tests

`tests/unit_test/app_common/logging/job_log_receiver_test.py` — 3 new:

-
`test_register_fires_on_run_lifecycle_events[_system_start|_about_to_start_run|_start_run]`
—
  every trigger event invokes `register_stream_processing` with the
  expected channel/topic.
- `test_register_reregisters_on_each_event` — repeat triggers all
  re-register, no "registered once" latch.
- `test_register_event_handlers_cover_server_subprocess_path` —
  regression guard so `START_RUN` cannot be silently dropped from the
  trigger list again.

Existing security/test coverage (peer-identity routing, site
`allow_log_streaming` enforcement) unchanged.

## Verified locally

- `pytest tests/unit_test/app_common/logging
tests/unit_test/app_common/streamers -v`
  → **50 passed** (Python 3.10.17, pytest 7.4.3).
- `black`, `isort`, `flake8` clean on changed files.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: license + style + full unit test suite green on the 2.8 base.
- [ ] Manual: run an auth_test-style integration job; confirm
      `grep "no stream processing info registered" /tmp/.../log.txt`
      returns no lines after the fix and that
      `JobLogReceiver - Saving live log` lines appear for both the
      in-job stream and the post-completion error_log upload.

commits.subject: Enhance CLI agent readiness workflows (#4500)
commits.body:
## Summary

This PR expands the NVFlare CLI for agent-friendly and
automation-friendly workflows. It adds stable JSON contracts, scoped
startup-kit selection, retry-safe job submission, bounded and
study-aware job operations, blocking job wait, JSONL job monitor
streaming, POC readiness/endpoint metadata, study submit-preflight
metadata, recipe metadata discovery, durable client disable/enable
workflows, and system lifecycle commands with structured output.

Current scope: **94 files changed**: **14 docs/design/user-guide
files**, **34 implementation files**, and **46 test files**.

## Key Design Decisions

- **Per-command identity selection is optional and non-mutating.**
Online commands use the active startup kit by default. If `--kit-id` or
`--startup-kit` is provided, it overrides the active startup kit for
that command only and does not change the human default startup kit.
- **Submit retry safety is token based.** `--submit-token` is scoped by
`study + submitter + token`; it is not an auth credential and does not
grant access.
- **No special `study=all` behavior.** Study selection is either omitted
for default behavior or set to an explicit study name.
- **Streaming output uses JSONL, not multi-object JSON.** `job monitor
--format jsonl` emits one complete JSON event per line; regular
`--format json` remains a single-envelope contract.
- **Startup-kit registry commands are flattened under `nvflare
config`.** The canonical commands are `nvflare config
add/use/inspect/list/remove`; no nested `config kit` command is
documented for this PR.
- **`config inspect` is read-only and human-readable.** It uses the same
table shape as `config list` for the active startup kit, plus the config
file path. JSON mode keeps the structured automation payload.
- **Human and machine output are separated.** Commands enhanced in this
PR keep JSON stdout as a single envelope and avoid leaking raw dict/list
output into human mode.
- **POC operations are local workspace operations.** `poc add-site` and
`poc add-user` do not require an active project-admin startup kit
because POC models local deployment setup, not production authorization.
- **POC port preflight is best effort.** It checks loopback availability
only and reports `scope: "loopback"` plus a note instead of binding
wildcard interfaces.
- **Recipe discovery is local installed-package discovery.** `recipe
list/show` do not connect to a FLARE server. Human mode prints a short
loading message before local import/inspection; JSON mode remains clean.
- **Recipe metadata is descriptive, not an absolute compatibility
contract.** `privacy` means a privacy feature is enabled/declared by
that recipe entry; lack of privacy metadata does not mean the underlying
algorithm cannot be combined with PETs. `state_exchange` text identifies
default transfer behavior when a recipe supports configurable transfer
types.
- **Client disable/enable is durable policy; `remove-client` is not
supported in the new `nvflare system` CLI surface.** `disable-client`
persists a disabled-client flag and rejects future heartbeats;
`enable-client` clears that flag so the client can rejoin.
- **`--schema` stays backward compatible.** Existing argparse-derived
schema data remains, with added behavioral metadata for agent-facing
commands.

## CLI Feature Changes

### Startup Kit / Identity Selection

Adds optional per-command selectors for online commands:

```bash
nvflare job list --kit-id <id>
nvflare job submit -j <job_folder> --startup-kit <path>
nvflare study list --kit-id <id>
nvflare system status --startup-kit <path>
```

`--kit-id` and `--startup-kit` are not required. If neither is provided,
the command uses normal startup-kit resolution, ending with the
configured active startup kit. If either selector is provided, it takes
precedence for that one command and does not mutate
`startup_kits.active` in `~/.nvflare/config.conf`.

`nvflare config list --format json` and `nvflare config inspect --format
json` provide stable startup-kit metadata for automation, including
identity, role/org/project when available, certificate expiration
status, and non-fatal findings for stale/unreadable kits.

`nvflare config inspect` human output uses the same table columns as
`config list`, scoped to the active startup kit:

```text
active  id                status  identity          cert_role      path
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
*       admin@nvidia.com  ok      admin@nvidia.com  project_admin  /private/tmp/nvflare/poc/example_project/prod_00/admin@nvidia.com

config_file: /Users/chesterc/.nvflare/config.conf
```

`nvflare config use` remains a human-facing convenience command that
mutates global CLI state. JSON mode returns a structured `startup_kit`
and `identity` payload plus a finding that automation should prefer
`--kit-id` or `--startup-kit`.

Startup-kit registry commands are:

```bash
nvflare config add <id> <startup-kit-dir>
nvflare config use <id>
nvflare config inspect
nvflare config list
nvflare config remove <id>
```

### Job Submit / Retry Recovery

Adds optional retry-safe submit-token recovery:

```bash
nvflare job submit -j <job_folder> [--study <name>] [--submit-token <token>] --format json
nvflare job list --study <name> --submit-token <token> --format json
```

`--submit-token` is caller-generated and optional. If it is omitted,
NVFlare does not auto-create a token: submit behavior remains unchanged,
each submit creates a new job as before, and the server still tracks the
accepted job through the normal job store/job history. No retry-safe
submit-token record is created, so `job list --submit-token` recovery is
available only when the original submit used a caller-provided token.

If a token is provided, submit-token records are scoped by `study +
submitter + token`, persisted with job state, and checked against the
canonical submitted job content. A retry with the same token and same
content returns the existing accepted job; a retry with the same token
and different content is rejected.

### Job Wait / Monitor

Adds blocking wait:

```bash
nvflare job wait <job_id> [--study <name>] [--timeout N] [--interval N] --format json
```

This blocks until terminal job state or timeout and returns one final
structured envelope. Human mode now prints periodic status context,
including the selected study, instead of only printing the initial
connection line.

Adds newline-delimited streaming monitor output:

```bash
nvflare job monitor <job_id> [--study <name>] [--timeout N] [--interval N] --format jsonl
```

- Each stdout line is a complete JSON object and is flushed immediately
for pipe consumers.
- Progress events use `terminal: false`.
- Final events use `event: "terminal"` and `terminal: true`.
- Timeout emits `status: "TIMEOUT"` and exits with code 3.
- Successful raw statuses such as `FINISHED_OK` normalize to `status:
"COMPLETED"` while preserving the raw value as `job_status`.
- JSONL is scoped to `job monitor`; non-streaming commands reject it.

### Job Metadata / Download / Logs

`job meta` is study-aware and has improved human output. Human mode now
renders grouped job details instead of raw key/value dumps, including
identity, status, execution, deployment, schedule attempts, and storage
details. JSON mode remains structured.

Job lookup failures for study-aware commands report the searched study
and hint to retry with `--study <study_name>` when appropriate, instead
of only saying the job does not exist.

`job download --format json` reports local artifact discovery under the
JSON `data` object. Human output remains concise and prints the final
download path. `--force` replaces an existing local download directory.

```json
{
  "data": {
    "download_path": "...",
    "path": "...",
    "artifact_discovery": "completed",
    "artifacts": {},
    "missing_artifacts": []
  }
}
```

`job logs` supports named studies and bounded output for automation:

```bash
nvflare job logs <job_id> [--study <name>] --site server|<client>|all --tail N --since <timestamp> --max-bytes N
```

`--study` defaults to `default`. For named-study jobs, callers must pass
the same study used for submit/list; otherwise `JOB_NOT_FOUND` reports
the searched study and hints to rerun with `--study <study_name>`.

Log retrieval now selects a single preferred log representation instead
of returning duplicate formats:

- `--format json` requests `log.json` first and falls back to `log.txt`
only when the JSON log is unavailable.
- Human mode requests `log.txt` first and falls back to `log.json`;
JSON-log fallback is rendered as text for display.
- Bounds (`--tail`, `--since`, `--max-bytes`) are applied by the CLI
after retrieval.

The log bounds are CLI-side bounds over server-side stored logs; the
command does not execute shell commands on client machines.

### POC Prepare / Start / Stop / Add

`poc prepare` reports startup-kit transition metadata and port-preflight
diagnostics in JSON mode without dumping agent diagnostics into human
output.

`poc start` waits for readiness by default and reports actual endpoint
metadata. Human output is concise and explains that the admin console is
optional.

`poc stop` has an explicit automation contract: by default it waits for
coordinated server shutdown and returns `status: stopped`; with
`--no-wait`, it returns after requesting shutdown with `status:
shutdown_initiated`.

`poc add-site` and `poc add-user` are explicit local workspace
modification commands. They replace the overloaded `poc add` shape for
the new CLI UX and do not require an active project-admin startup kit.
Adding a second POC project-admin user is rejected because the generated
POC workspace has a single project admin.

`poc start` endpoint metadata:

```json
{
  "server_address": "localhost:8002",
  "admin_address": "localhost:8003",
  "ready_timeout": 30,
  "port_conflict": false,
  "port_preflight": {},
  "warnings": [],
  "ready": true
}
```

`server_address` and `admin_address` are the source of truth for
follow-on automation.

### Study List

`study list --format json` returns startup-kit metadata plus
authenticated identity/study details from the server, including
role/capability fields such as `can_submit_job`.

`can_submit_job` is derived from the server authorization service
instead of hard-coded role checks in the CLI. Human output is rendered
as readable identity/startup-kit text plus a study table instead of raw
Python dict/list formatting.

Example response shape:

```json
{
  "startup_kit": {"source": "active", "id": "...", "path": "..."},
  "identity": {"name": "...", "org": "...", "role": "..."},
  "studies": ["..."],
  "study_details": [
    {
      "name": "...",
      "role": "...",
      "capabilities": {"submit_job": true},
      "can_submit_job": true
    }
  ]
}
```

This is membership-level submit preflight. Hidden or unmapped studies
are omitted; full future policy introspection remains out of scope.

### Recipe Discovery

Adds filterable/queryable recipe metadata:

```bash
nvflare recipe list [--framework <framework>] [--filter key=value] --format json
nvflare recipe show <name> --format json
```

Supported filter keys are `framework`, `privacy`, `algorithm`,
`aggregation`, and `state_exchange`. The user guide and design doc now
list the available values for each metadata key, show which frameworks
each value applies to, and include examples for common combinations.

Human mode now prints progress while local recipe metadata is loaded:

```text
Loading installed recipe catalog...
Loading installed recipe metadata for 'fedavg'...
```

The `recipe show` human summary distinguishes enabled privacy features
from metadata declarations and clarifies default/configurable state
exchange. For example:

```text
state_exchange: full_model (default; params_transfer_type=FULL, supports FULL or DIFF)
privacy: none enabled by default
privacy compatibility: not declared in recipe metadata
parameters: 28 available; run 'nvflare recipe show fedavg --format json'
```

JSON output remains the full structured metadata contract, including
algorithm, aggregation, state exchange, framework support, privacy
compatibility, constructor parameters, optional dependencies, and
template references.

### CLI Schema Contract Metadata

Agent-facing commands add behavior metadata to `--schema` output:

```json
{
  "output_modes": ["json"],
  "streaming": false,
  "mutating": false,
  "idempotent": true,
  "retry_token": {"supported": false}
}
```

Initial coverage includes `job
submit/list/meta/wait/monitor/download/logs`, `config use/inspect/list`,
`recipe list/show`, and `study list`.

For retry-safe submit commands:

```json
{
  "retry_token": {
    "supported": true,
    "flag": "--submit-token",
    "scope": "study + submitter + token",
    "retry_safe_when_present": true,
    "effect": "Deduplicates retries for identical submitted job content in the same study by the same submitter; different content with the same token is rejected."
  }
}
```

For streaming monitor:

```json
{
  "output_modes": ["json", "jsonl"],
  "streaming": true,
  "mutating": false,
  "idempotent": true
}
```

### System Lifecycle

Adds structured lifecycle behavior:

```bash
nvflare system shutdown <server|client|all> [--no-wait] --format json
nvflare system restart <server|client|all> [--no-wait] --format json
nvflare system disable-client <client_name> --format json
nvflare system enable-client <client_name> --format json
```

`shutdown` and `restart` support wait/no-wait behavior for automation.
No-wait machine statuses use underscore values: `shutdown_initiated` and
`restart_initiated`.

`disable-client` persists a disabled-client flag and rejects future
heartbeats until `enable-client` clears it. `enable-client` removes the
disabled flag so the client can rejoin on its next heartbeat/session
attempt. `remove-client` is intentionally not exposed as a supported
`nvflare system` CLI command; durable exclusion should use
`disable-client`.

## Major Bug Fixes and Hardening

This section lists fixes relative to the previous PR/baseline. It
intentionally does not enumerate review-round fixes for features
introduced inside this PR.

- Fixed `job monitor` not being study-aware; it now supports `--study`
and uses the selected study session.
- Fixed `job logs` not being study-aware; it now supports `--study` and
reports the searched study on `JOB_NOT_FOUND`.
- Replaced the misleading non-durable `system remove-client` workflow in
the new CLI surface with durable `disable-client` / `enable-client`
semantics.
- Fixed user-submitted jobs being able to carry `from_hub_site`
metadata. User submissions now strip `from_hub_site`, so only the
server-side `HubAppDeployer` can mark HUB-created jobs and trigger
HUB-specific signature-verification behavior.
- Hardened cert request and signed-zip validation to reject private key
material embedded in zip members, including PEM content hidden in `.pem`
files.
- Hardened certificate generation helpers to reject duplicate or
reserved X.509 extensions and validate CA `not_valid_before` in addition
to expiration.
- Fixed invalid CLI connection-timeout values to fall back to the
default with a warning instead of failing unexpectedly.

Docs updated for:

- `nvflare config inspect` naming and table-style human output.

errors.

This PR updates the Kubernetes job launcher to run launched jobs without
mounting the shared workspace PVC.

Instead, launched jobs now:
- mount `startup/` from a Secret
- use an `emptyDir` as their writable workspace
- download `local/` and the job workspace over CellNet/F3 before startup
- upload job results back to the parent over the same path on shutdown

This preserves `local/` workspace behavior while isolating each launched
job's writable workspace.

commits.subject: Fix JobRunner completion context race (#4471)
commits.body:
## Summary
This PR fixes a server-side race in JobRunner when completed jobs are
processed concurrently with scheduling.

The completion thread was reusing the scheduling loop's FLContext, and
both paths mutate FLContextKey.CURRENT_JOB_ID. Under concurrent jobs,
that could fire JOB_COMPLETED with the wrong job id, leaving completed
jobs stuck in DefaultJobScheduler.scheduled_jobs and blocking later jobs
from being scheduled.

## Changes
- pass engine into the completion thread instead of the shared FLContext
- create a fresh engine.new_context() for each completed job before
firing JOB_COMPLETED
- add a regression test covering completion-event context isolation

## Validation
- tests/unit_test/private/fed/server/job_runner_test.py

commits.subject: Add distributed provisioning: nvflare cert/package CLI + runtime security fixes (#4380)
commits.body:
## Summary

Implements distributed provisioning for NVFlare — an inverted-trust
workflow where each
site generates its own RSA private key locally. Only CSRs are exchanged
out-of-band; the
Project Admin never handles any site private key. The produced startup
kits are structurally
identical to centrally provisioned kits at runtime.

## New CLI Commands

- **`nvflare cert init`** — Project Admin bootstraps the root CA
(one-time per federation).
  Produces `rootCA.pem`, `rootCA.key` (0600), `ca.json`.
- **`nvflare cert csr`** — Site Admin generates RSA key + CSR locally.
Types: `client`,
`server`, `org_admin`, `lead`, `member`. Private key never leaves the
machine.
- **`nvflare cert sign`** — Project Admin signs a received CSR with the
root CA. The `-t`
type arg is authoritative — CSR role field is ignored (prevents
privilege escalation).
- **`nvflare package`** — Site Admin assembles a startup kit from their
local key + the
signed cert + rootCA.pem received from the Project Admin. Supports
`--dir` auto-discovery
  or explicit `--cert/--key/--rootca` paths.

All commands support `--output json` (machine-readable), `--output
quiet`, and `--schema`
(prints JSON schema for the command and exits).

## Runtime Security Fixes

| Fix | File | Change |
|-----|------|--------|
| D1 | `lighter/impl/signature.py` | Stop generating `signature.json`
for non-CC, non-HE kits — mTLS is the trust anchor for plain kits |
| D2 | `fed/utils/fed_utils.py` | Gate startup integrity check on
`valid_config` (not just `secure_train`) — prevents false abort when
`signature.json` is absent |
| D3 | `fed/server/job_runner.py`, `fed/client/training_cmds.py`,
`hub/hub_app_deployer.py`, `fed/server/job_cmds.py` | Job signature
verification now checks `__nvfl_sig.json` presence +
`require_signed_jobs` policy instead of `secure_train`; strips
`FROM_HUB_SITE` from user-submitted job meta to prevent privilege
escalation |
| D4 | `fuel/hci/client/file_transfer.py` | Guard `push_folder` signing
behind key-file existence check — simulator mode no longer errors on
missing key |
| D5 | `fuel/hci/client/config.py` | `secure_load_admin_config` allows
`NOT_SIGNED` when `valid_config=False` — admin login works for manual
workflow and non-CC kits |
| D6 | `fed/server/job_runner.py` | Add
`_require_signed_jobs(workspace)` helper: reads `fed_server.json`,
defaults to `True` when `rootCA.pem` present |

## New Infrastructure

- `nvflare/tool/cli_output.py` — `output()` / `output_error()` with
json/quiet/human-readable rendering
- `nvflare/tool/cli_errors.py` — centralized error code registry with
template messages and hints
- `nvflare/tool/cli_schema.py` — `parser_to_schema()` generates JSON
schema from argparse definitions

## Test Coverage

215 unit tests added across 12 new test files. All pass.

- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/unit_test/tool/ -v` — CLI + cert +
package (186 tests)
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest
tests/unit_test/lighter/test_signature_builder.py -v` — D1 (7 tests)
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/unit_test/fuel/hci/client/ -v` — D4 + D5
(13 tests)
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/unit_test/private/fed/ -v` — D2 + D3 + D6
(9 + 8 + 21 + 9 tests)

`package` → site start

commits.subject: Cherry-pick [2.7] Fix hierarchical FL startup failures: deployment timeouts, selective client exclusion, and dead-detection debounce (#4209) (#4288)
commits.body:
## Problem

Large-scale hierarchical FL jobs (e.g. BERT NER, 144 clients, 6 relays
on Frontier) abort in
Round 0 due to a cascading startup failure chain.  The root sequence is:

1. F3 streaming HOL stall (PR #4206) delays deployment ACKs from
relay-connected clients
2. **`_deploy_job()`** treats `reply=None` (timeout) as `"unknown"` —
not a failure — so
   timed-out clients silently appear to have been deployed
3. **`_start_run()`** tries to start those clients; they again time out,
and
   `check_client_replies()` ignores the `None` reply
4. **`_sync_client_jobs()`** fires dead-job notification on the very
first heartbeat with
   no startup grace period
5. FedAvg requires 144/144 — one or two missing clients → abort
6. A late-starting CJ crashes with `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not
iterable` when
`get_job_clients()` receives `None` metadata from an already-aborted job

PRs #4206, #4204, #4174, #4172, #4186, #4211, #4210 (all merged in
2.7.2) address the
transport layer.  This PR addresses the remaining job lifecycle layer.

---

## Fixes Included

### 1 — `_deploy_job()`: Treat deployment timeout as failure
(`job_runner.py`)

**Root bug**: `reply=None` was logged as `"unknown"` and excluded from
`failed_clients`,
so timed-out clients counted as "successfully deployed" for the
`min_sites` check.

**Fix**: Add timed-out clients to `failed_clients` with a `"deployment
timeout"` label.
The existing `min_sites` / `required_sites` logic then correctly decides
whether to abort.

### 2 — `check_client_replies()`: Return timed-out clients instead of
raising (`admin.py`)

**Root bug**: In strict mode, any timeout raised immediately, aborting
the whole job even
when the remaining active clients satisfied `min_sites`.

**Fix**: In strict mode, collect timed-out clients into a return list
rather than raising.
Explicit errors (non-OK return code or error body) still raise. Also
fixes the non-strict
mode to use name-keyed dict lookup instead of fragile positional
`zip()`.

New signature: `check_client_replies(...) -> List[str]` (timed-out
client names; empty = none).

### 3 — `_start_run()`: Selective exclusion with min_sites re-evaluation
(`job_runner.py`)

**Root bug**: A start-job timeout under strict mode aborted the entire
job with no
tolerance for stragglers within `min_sites` bounds.

**Fix**: Use the returned timed-out list from `check_client_replies()`.
If remaining
active clients >= `min_sites`, log a warning and proceed. Only abort
when below tolerance.

### 4 — `_sync_client_jobs()`: Require-prior-report default changed to
`True` (`fed_server.py`)

**Root bug**: `SYNC_CLIENT_JOBS_REQUIRE_PREVIOUS_REPORT` defaulted to
`False`, meaning
the bug fix was opt-in and the unsafe behaviour remained the default.

**Fix**: Default changed to `True`. Operators who want the aggressive
legacy detection
can set it to `False` explicitly.

### 5 — `_sync_client_jobs()`: Move `_reported_clients` out of
`job_info` dict (`fed_server.py`)

**Root bug**: Positive-observation tracking was stored as
`job_info["_reported_clients"]`,
injecting algorithm state into a data dict with no corresponding
`RunProcessKey` constant.

**Fix**: Tracking moved to `self._job_reported_clients: Dict[str, set]`
on `FederatedServer`.
Stale entries are purged whenever a job is no longer in `run_processes`.

### 6 — `ClientRunManager.get_job_clients()`: Explicit meta validation
(`client_run_manager.py`)

Raises `RuntimeError` with a descriptive message instead of an opaque
`TypeError` when
`JOB_CLIENTS` is absent or the wrong type.

---

## Configuration Recommendations (No Code Change Needed)

| Setting | Recommended value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `FedAvg(min_clients=...)` | 96-98% of `num_clients` | Tolerates a few
startup stragglers |
| `runner_sync_timeout` | `120` s | Allows Lustre-backed deployments
time to complete |
| `strict_start_job_reply_check` | `true` | Start-job timeouts surfaced,
straggler clients excluded |
| `sync_client_jobs_require_previous_report` | `true` (now the default)
| Prevents premature dead-job from startup delay | |
`SFM_CLOSE_STALLED_CONNECTION` (PR #4206) | `true` after staging |
Disconnects stalled relay connections |

---

## Files Changed

- `nvflare/private/fed/server/job_runner.py` — `_deploy_job()` timeout
as failure; `_start_run()` selective exclusion
- `nvflare/private/fed/server/admin.py` — `check_client_replies()`
returns timed-out list; dict-keyed non-strict path
- `nvflare/private/fed/server/fed_server.py` — `_sync_client_jobs()`
default `True`; `_job_reported_clients` attr; stale cleanup
- `nvflare/private/fed/client/client_run_manager.py` — explicit meta
validation in `get_job_clients()`

---

## Test Coverage

New and updated unit tests with both positive and negative cases:

| File | Tests | What they cover |
|---|---|---|
| `admin_test.py` | 8 | Timeout returned not raised; dict lookup; error
still raises; reorder OK |
| `job_runner_test.py` | 4 | strict flag wiring; timeout within
tolerance → warn; timeout below tolerance → raise | |
`job_runner_deploy_test.py` | 9 (new file) | Timeout counted as failure;
OK reply not failed; mixed outcomes; detail label; min_sites with
timeouts; integration sequence |
| `fed_server_test.py` | 5 | Default requires-prior-report; legacy
explicit-False still fires; tracking in server attr not job_info; stale
cleanup |

All 29 targeted unit tests pass.

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests for each changed function (positive + negative)
- [x] New `job_runner_deploy_test.py` covering deployment timeout
classification end-to-end
- [x] All 29 targeted unit tests pass
- [ ] Hierarchical staging run with all flags at default
- [ ] Hierarchical staging run with `strict_start_job_reply_check=true`
and reduced `min_clients`
- [ ] Verify no regression on standard (non-hierarchical) FL jobs

commits.subject: Get job participating clients from Job Meta (#3270)
commits.body:
Fixes # .

### Description

At the start of a job, the CJ sends a sync message to the server to get
information about the job's participating clients. This mechanism has a
few issues:

- CJs are started at about the same time. If there are many clients
(e.g. there could be thousands of clients for handling edge devices),
the SP will be under a lot of pressure to process so many messages at
the same time.

- In case of Simulator, if the number of subprocesses is smaller than
the number of clients, then some clients will be swapped in and out.
Each time a client is swapped in, it needs to send the sync message
again. But if this happens after the job is already done, it will fail,
as reported by QA.

This PR gets rid of the sync mechanism from CJs. Once the SP starts to
run a job, it already knows what clients will participate in the job. SP
then includes such info in the job's metadata in the message to CPs to
start the job. Once started, the CJ no longer needs to send the sync
message to SP to get participating clients since it can get this info
from the job's metadata.

This PR also cleans up some log messages by changing their log level to
DEBUG.

NOTE: this PR does not change SJ's logic to get job clients from SP via
the sync message, due to the large scope of changes. Since there is
always only a single SJ for each job, it won't cost much for the SP to
process one message from the SJ.

Fixes # .

### Description

This PR adds support of client hierarchy, which is needed to support
edge device applications.

- The Provision tool has been enhanced such that a "parent" property can
be specified for a client. The "parent" of a client is another
provisioned client. Circular parent/child relationship is detected and
prohibited. Once provisioned, the client's fed_client.json is augmented
with the client's FQSN (fully qualified site name), which specifies the
client's position in the client hierarchy.

client's parent (instead of Server) for task and job-related
interactions (pull task, submit result, sync runner, job heartbeat,

the server need to pull tasks.

used for hierarchical aggregations based on client hierarchy. This
executor must be used if client hierarchy is defined.

FLContext to the same value. Currently the two keys have different
values, but some code has been misusing them (set with one key and get

error-prone. Also defined methods for both Shareable and FLContext for
setting and getting peer context, and refactored code to use these

commits.subject: Support relay - Part 1 (#3198)
commits.body:
Fixes # .

### Description

This PR implements support of using relays in building NVFLARE cellnet.
Relays are nodes in the cellnet that are only used for routing messages.
They do not have any learning functions.

This is the Part 1 of the relay support. It does not include
provisioning functions for creating startup kits for relays. These
functions will be done in future PRs.

Just like regular clients, relays also register to the Server when they
are started. Once successfully registered, the Server sends auth token
and signature to the relay.

Relay nodes also perform message authentication: relays validate auth
headers for all messages going thru them. Since all cross-site messages
must go thru either the server or relays (or both), by enforcing message
authentication at both the Server and relays ensure that no cross-site
messages can go through without valid auth headers.

Currently peers of a CellPipe can only communicate via the Server. This
PR includes an enhancement that allows peers to communicate via CP or
Relay nodes. This can make the peer-to-peer communication more
efficient.
